cards.title: PMAY-U 2.0 includes project infrastructure
cards.text: The September 2024 guidelines distinguish a completed dwelling from a completed project with infrastructure. Unified MIS, geotagging and monitoring are specified. These are documented requirements, not a test of local implementation.

cards.title: Four PMAY-U 2.0 verticals
cards.text: The four verticals are Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS). Legacy ISSR is not an additional fifth 2.0 vertical. Individual entitlement requires applicable current rules and competent authority review.

cards.title: SBM already specifies functional-asset monitoring
cards.text: The October 2021 SBM-U 2.0 guidelines specify functional-asset monitoring, ICT/GIS evaluation and an integrated platform for city/ward profiles, infrastructure and sanitation/waste progress. Indexed Chapter 10 was read; the full PDF was not acquired. Local effectiveness is untested.

cards.title: Citizen confirmation and reopening already exist
cards.text: An official PIB description of Swachhata documents photo/location reports, ward assignment, notifications and a seven-day citizen confirmation/reopening window. A new geo-photo complaint app cannot claim this capability as new. No local resolution rate was measured.

cards.title: SRA GIS has existing multi-layer mapping
cards.text: NIC describes existing SRA GIS and AASRA with more than ten layers, including wards, villages, slum clusters and rehabilitation schemes. Documentation does not establish a successful current export or complete household-service data.

cards.title: SRA public rows identify locality leads
cards.text: The public SRA table includes Bharti CHS, Universal CHS and AHAD CHS & ITEHAD CHS in M-E/Govandi/Deonar with CTS 1-A. A shared CTS is not a unique scheme join. Listing presence and blank proposal fields establish neither delay nor completion status.
cards.observation_period: Record update date unknown; accessed 17 October 2026

cards.title: M/E water and toilet context is historical
cards.text: Census 2011 ward-wide household measures reproduced in the 2022 climate plan are: treated tap water 82.8%, tap within premises 53.6%, latrine within premises 35.8%. These are not slum-only or current figures. No private latrine is not the same as no toilet; these figures do not measure uptime or water quality.

cards.title: BMC reports Water for All from May 2022
cards.text: BMC's 2025 year book reports an inclusive Water for All policy from May 2022 covering slums and unauthorised non-slum areas, among others. This qualifies older accounts of exclusion. A policy announcement does not establish universal reliable supply.

cards.title: Housing shortage is a dated estimate
cards.text: The 2012 TG-12 estimate was 18.78 million nationally and 1.94 million for Maharashtra. It includes congestion and obsolescence as well as homelessness; it is not a current ward shortage or simply a count of absent buildings.

cards.title: Slum population anchors are Census 2011
cards.text: The official historical table records 65,494,604 slum residents nationally and 11,848,423 in Maharashtra in Census 2011. The figures are not a 2026 enumeration or an M/E population estimate.

cards.title: Census HL-04 covers historical ownership and rooms
cards.text: Catalogue 11441 is SLUM HL-04: Slum households by ownership status of the census houses, size of the household and number of dwelling rooms — 2011, reference PC11_SLUM_HL04. India/State aggregates and SHH1604-crc.pdf are advertised. Metadata was verified; the PDF was not downloaded. Ownership categories do not decide legal tenure or eligibility.

cards.title: OSM data and service performance are different evidence
cards.text: OpenStreetMap data are available under ODbL with attribution and applicable database obligations. Crowdsourced mapped presence does not establish facility hours, capacity, accessibility or reliable service. Tile and API use policies are separate.

cards.title: Three transport points are secondary references
cards.text: Mapcarta's OSM-derived records locate Govandi railway station, Bainganwadi bus stop and Shivaji Nagar Bus Depot. Observation dates and passenger entrances were not verified; the depot point represents a way. No road network, timetable or service coverage was obtained.

cards.title: Policy recognises stalled redevelopment
cards.text: Maharashtra Housing Policy 2025 recognises developer financial stress, stalled redevelopment and delayed transit rent. Its account records 228 MMR projects selected for a joint-venture route. This is a policy snapshot, not today's total stalled count or an M/E project status.

papers.title: Enabling Slum Redevelopment in Mumbai: Policy Paradox in Practice
papers.metadata: **Vinit Mukhija (2001). Housing Studies 16(6), 791–806.** DOI: [10.1080/02673030120090548](https://doi.org/10.1080/02673030120090548). [Publisher record and abstract](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/02673030120090548). Access: ABSTRACT; full publisher retrieval failed. The volume year is 2001 despite later online-posting metadata.

fields.Area / question: Mumbai; what does enabling market-led slum redevelopment require from the state?
fields.Data / sample: Redevelopment programme evidence; exact cases/interview sample not verified from accessible abstract.
fields.Method: Case-based policy argument; detailed protocol inaccessible.
fields.Findings: Market delivery can require coordinated authority, public investment and regulation.
fields.Limitations: Historical institutional setting; no current programme-effect estimate. Abstract access limits detailed appraisal.
fields.Relevance: Identifies governance/finance dependencies that an application cannot remove through digitisation alone.

papers.title: Experiences with surveying and mapping Pune and Sangli slums on a geographical information system (GIS)
papers.metadata: **Pratima Joshi, Srinanda Sen and Jane Hobson (2002). Environment and Urbanization 14(2), 225–240.** DOI: [10.1177/095624780201400218](https://doi.org/10.1177/095624780201400218). [Full paper](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/095624780201400218). Access: FULL.

fields.Area / question: Pune and Sangli; can community-produced spatial information support inclusive planning?
fields.Data / sample: Household surveys, settlement/service maps and development plans; not a random national sample.
fields.Method: Participatory enumeration, GIS overlays and comparative institutional experience.
fields.Findings: Useful planning information was produced, with contrasting municipal uptake in the two cities.
fields.Limitations: Implementer-authored historical cases; evidence is descriptive rather than causal.
fields.Relevance: Direct prior art for community GIS and a warning that usable maps require organisational adoption.

papers.title: Off the map: the health and social implications of being a non-notified slum in India
papers.metadata: **Ramnath Subbaraman, Jennifer O’Brien, Tejal Shitole, Shrutika Shitole, Kiran Sawant, David E. Bloom and Anita Patil-Deshmukh (2012). Environment and Urbanization 24(2), 643–663.** DOI: [10.1177/0956247812456356](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956247812456356). [Full paper](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0956247812456356). Access: FULL.

fields.Area / question: Kaula Bandar, Mumbai; how does non-notification relate to service exclusion and health?
fields.Data / sample: Multiple studies: 959-household baseline, 6,063-person anthropometric survey, qualitative work and NFHS-3 comparisons.
fields.Method: Mixed-method comparative analysis and governance framework.
fields.Findings: The community showed severe service and health disadvantages.
fields.Limitations: Observational, one settlement, different survey periods and historical policy conditions.
fields.Relevance: Supports attention to institutional exclusion. Do not generalise its rates or old legal restrictions to present Mumbai. BMC reports a later Water for All policy.

papers.title: The social ecology of water in a Mumbai slum: failures in water quality, quantity, and reliability
papers.metadata: **Ramnath Subbaraman, Shrutika Shitole, Tejal Shitole, Kiran Sawant, Jennifer O’Brien, David E. Bloom and Anita Patil-Deshmukh (2013). BMC Public Health 13, 173.** DOI: [10.1186/1471-2458-13-173](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2458-13-173). [Publisher full text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1471-2458-13-173); [Harvard record](https://dash.harvard.edu/entities/publication/73120378-ae5c-6bd4-e053-0100007fdf3b). Access: FULL at publisher; PMC browser check and Harvard file retrieval failed.

fields.Area / question: Kaula Bandar; performance of an informal water-distribution system.
fields.Data / sample: 2008 baseline of 959 households; 2011 assessment of 229 water samples, including repeated sampling of 21 households.
fields.Method: Seasonal testing, cost/quantity assessment and logistic regression.
fields.Findings: Water availability, expense, source quality and household storage produced distinct problems.
fields.Limitations: Single historical community; baseline nonresponse and small repeated household sample.
fields.Relevance: Measure reliability, quantity, quality and affordability separately. A mapped pipe cannot validate potable supply.

papers.title: Defying NGO-ization?: Lessons in Livelihood Resilience Observed Among Involuntarily Displaced Women in Mumbai, India
papers.metadata: **Ramya Ramanath (2016). World Development 84, 1–17.** DOI: [10.1016/j.worlddev.2016.04.007](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.worlddev.2016.04.007). [Original publisher](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0305750X16303606); [author's university bibliographic record](https://scholars.depaul.edu/en/publications/defying-ngo-ization-lessons-in-livelihood-resilience-observed-amo/). Access: INDEXED-SECTIONS/abstract; direct full retrieval failed. University record confirms volume 84 and publication on 1 August 2016.

fields.Area / question: A Mumbai resettlement site; how do displaced women reconstruct livelihoods?
fields.Data / sample: 120 relocated women; exact site name and full sampling protocol not verified here.
fields.Findings: Residents developed varied livelihood strategies and exercised agency beyond institutional prescriptions.
fields.Limitations: One selected group; qualitative findings do not estimate city-wide income loss or relocation effects.
fields.Relevance: Include women's livelihood preferences and continuity in any scenario appraisal.

papers.title: Formalization, Citizenship and the Challenges of Self-Governance in Mumbai’s Slum Relocation Colonies
papers.metadata: **Robert J. Chaskin, Mouleshri Vyas and Manish K. Jha (2024). International Journal of Urban and Regional Research 48(6), 1115–1136.** DOI: [10.1111/1468-2427.13274](https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-2427.13274). [University repository](https://knowledge.uchicago.edu/records/c0z96-tzt75). Access: publisher methods/results exposed in indexed text; repository metadata read, PDF retrieval failed.

fields.Area / question: Majas and Lallubhai Compound, Mumbai; how does formal housing reshape local governance?
fields.Data / sample: 89 resident interviews, key informants and two years of observations; purposive sampling.
fields.Method: Comparative qualitative cases and thematic coding.
fields.Findings: Tenure/plumbing benefits coexisted with maintenance burdens and uneven participation and responsiveness.
fields.Limitations: Two cases, historical fieldwork and reported experiences; not a prevalence survey.
fields.Relevance: Post-handover governance matters. Service reporting must include renters and less powerful residents.

papers.title: An ontology of slums for image-based classification
papers.metadata: **Divyani Kohli, Richard Sliuzas, Norman Kerle and Alfred Stein (2012). Computers, Environment and Urban Systems 36(2), 154–163.** DOI: [10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2011.11.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2011.11.001). [Author institution](https://research.utwente.nl/en/publications/an-ontology-of-slums-for-image-based-classification/); [full article copy hosted by Uruguay's spatial-data authority](https://www.gub.uy/infraestructura-datos-espaciales/sites/infraestructura-datos-espaciales/files/documentos/noticias/Paper_Computers_Environment%20and%20Urban%20Systems.pdf). Access: FULL.

fields.Area / question: International expert input; Kisumu demonstration. How can morphological indicators support classification?
fields.Data / sample: 50 experts covering 16 countries and image-based example.
fields.Method: Generic ontology at object, settlement and environs scales; local object-oriented adaptation.
fields.Findings: Structured physical concepts aid image classification, with context-dependent appearance.
fields.Limitations: Physical proxies do not establish household rights, poverty or functioning services.
fields.Relevance: Separate morphological observations from legal and social attributes.

papers.title: Slums from Space—15 Years of Slum Mapping Using Remote Sensing
papers.metadata: **Monika Kuffer, Karin Pfeffer and Richard Sliuzas (2016). Remote Sensing 8(6), 455.** DOI: [10.3390/rs8060455](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs8060455). [Publisher](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/8/6/455); [institutional record](https://research.utwente.nl/en/publications/slums-from-space-15-years-of-slum-mapping-using-remote-sensing/). Access: INDEXED-SECTIONS, including review method; direct publisher open failed.

fields.Area / question: Global South; what remote-sensing approaches work across contexts?
fields.Data / sample: 87 key publications from 2000–2015; English-language search conducted December 2015.
fields.Method: Review of context, morphology, sensor requirements and extraction methods.
fields.Findings: Approaches and information scales vary; context and mapping dynamics remain important limitations.
fields.Limitations: Historical sensor/method literature, variable study protocols and publication selection.
fields.Relevance: An established field of prior art. New CV requires local labels and evaluation.

papers.title: Semantic segmentation of slums in satellite images using transfer learning on fully convolutional neural networks
papers.metadata: **Michael Wurm, Thomas Stark, Xiao Xiang Zhu, Matthias Weigand and Hannes Taubenböck (2019). ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 150, 59–69.** DOI: [10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2019.02.006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2019.02.006). [DLR record](https://elib.dlr.de/126606/). Access: ABSTRACT and indexed paper sections; full PDF request failed.

fields.Area / question: Slum-image test sites; exact spatial footprint not confirmed from accessed methods. Can FCNs transfer across sensors?
fields.Data / sample: QuickBird optical training imagery, Sentinel-2 and TerraSAR-X; exact split counts unverified.
fields.Method: FCN semantic segmentation with transfer learning.
fields.Findings: Optical transfer helped in the reported experiment; SAR transfer did not improve segmentation.
fields.Limitations: Sensor/domain dependence; local validation and image rights are prerequisites.
fields.Relevance: Feasibility evidence for morphology mapping, not proof of service-deficit detection. No published accuracy is claimed for this project.

papers.metadata: **M. Kuffer, D. R. Thomson, G. Boo, R. Mahabir, T. Grippa, S. Vanhuysse, R. Engstrom, R. Ndugwa, J. Makau, E. Darin, J. Porto de Albuquerque and C. Kabaria (2020). Remote Sensing 12(6), 982.** DOI: [10.3390/rs12060982](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12060982). [Glasgow record](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/256041/); [publisher](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/12/6/982). Access: ABSTRACT and indexed substantive sections; linked full PDF fetch failed. Initials follow verified repository metadata.

fields.Area / question: LMIC cities; how can census, community and EO approaches be combined?
fields.Data / sample: Review including 30 key post-2016 EO articles.
fields.Findings: Scalability, transferability, local context and validation remain challenges.
fields.Limitations: A proposed mapping framework does not establish local deployment effects.
fields.Relevance: Integrated participatory mapping is existing prior art; validate any incremental contribution.

papers.title: GIS-based multicriteria decision analysis: a survey of the literature
papers.metadata: **Jacek Malczewski (2006). International Journal of Geographical Information Science 20(7), 703–726.** DOI: [10.1080/13658810600661508](https://doi.org/10.1080/13658810600661508). [Publisher](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/13658810600661508). Access: ABSTRACT and indexed metadata; direct PDF retrieval failed. Journal year is 2006, despite later online-posting metadata.

fields.Area / question: International literature; what forms of GIS-MCDA have developed?
fields.Findings: GIS and multi-criteria methods have a substantial established literature.
fields.Limitations: Not an empirical validation of housing priorities; historical method coverage.
fields.Relevance: Transparent weighting is a sensible baseline. Weight choice remains normative and needs stakeholder agreement and sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: Stop explaining black box machine learning models for high stakes decisions and use interpretable models instead
papers.metadata: **Cynthia Rudin (2019). Nature Machine Intelligence 1, 206–215.** DOI: [10.1038/s42256-019-0048-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-019-0048-x). [Author manuscript](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1811.10154), arXiv:1811.10154, version dated September 2019. Access: FULL author manuscript; publisher page fetch failed. Publication identity was checked against the author/repository and publisher-indexed citation.

fields.Area / question: General high-stakes ML; whether post-hoc explanation is an adequate substitute for interpretable models.
fields.Data / sample: Conceptual argument and application examples, not a new Maharashtra sample.
fields.Findings: Post-hoc explanations may fail to reflect the original model faithfully.
fields.Limitations: No housing-specific effect estimate or universal proof that simple models always win.
fields.Relevance: Prefer auditable rules when sufficient; explanation does not legitimise automated housing decisions.

papers.title: A Rapid Assessment Scorecard to Identify Informal Settlements at Higher Maternal and Child Health Risk in Mumbai
papers.metadata: **David Osrin, Sushmita Das, Ujwala Bapat, Glyn A. Alcock, Wasundhara Joshi and Neena Shah More (2011). Journal of Urban Health 88(5), 919–932.** DOI: [10.1007/s11524-011-9556-7](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11524-011-9556-7). [Publisher full text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11524-011-9556-7). Access: FULL.

fields.Area / question: 48 clusters in six Mumbai wards; can observable conditions help prioritise health action?
fields.Data / sample: 10,754 births with detailed data from 2005–2007 surveillance.
fields.Method: Logistic regression, classification/regression trees and a six-indicator triage scorecard.
fields.Findings: Some environmental attributes associated with vulnerability; scorecard sensitivity and positive predictive value were limited.
fields.Limitations: Selected vulnerable clusters and limited external validity; not a redevelopment ranking trial.
fields.Relevance: Strong local prior art for prioritisation and a reason to test false negatives, not just attractive rankings.

papers.title: Life between the city and the village: Scaling analysis of service access in Indian urban slums
papers.metadata: **Anand Sahasranaman and Luís M. A. Bettencourt (2021). World Development 142, 105435.** DOI: [10.1016/j.worlddev.2021.105435](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.worlddev.2021.105435). [Publisher identity/abstract](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0305750X21000474); [author-institution publication list](https://voices.uchicago.edu/miurbandev/our-publications/). Access: INDEXED-SECTIONS for final journal metadata/abstract; direct publisher request returned 403. The [2019 author preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.05728), titled “Life Between the City and the Village: Comparative Analysis of Service Access in Indian Urban Slums,” was read in FULL. Methods below refer to that manuscript; changes in the final journal methods were not audited. The versions count as one work.

fields.Area / question: Four ULBs in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh; beneficiary experiences under BLC.
fields.Data / sample: Approximately 200 beneficiaries; household enquiry and group discussions.
fields.Method: Pilot assessment comparing reported previous/current conditions across livelihood dimensions.
fields.Findings: Housing/security gains coexisted with neighbourhood amenity gaps and informal borrowing.
fields.Limitations: Programme-authored, small selected sample, recall/comparison limitations; not causal or Maharashtra-representative.
fields.Relevance: Includes positive counterevidence and supports evaluation beyond dwelling counts.
